solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Enchant? Church might (5)

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
might or power, as in the long arm of the law

annotation.surface: A question about whether a church could cast a spell.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue: 'Enchant?' is the definition, and 'Church might' reads like an answer to it but is two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to charm and to enchant both originally meant casting a spell, and both now mean delighting someone.

entries.clue: Disgusted by repeated fine after Lancashire possibly cheat (7,3)

indicators.note: something repeated appears twice, so fine's F is written two times
what comes after is placed later in the answer, so FF follows CHEESE and DO

blocks.note: Lancashire is a type of English cheese; 'possibly' marks it as an example
to do someone is to cheat them

annotation.surface: Someone upset by a Lancashire cheat who keeps getting fined.
annotation.walkthrough: Lancashire reads as the English county but is the crumbly cheese named after it.
annotation.definitionFit: A British informal idiom: cheesed off means fed up or annoyed, close enough to disgusted in the sense of exasperated.

entries.clue: Affirmed removing leader’s support (3)

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and removing it takes S off SAID

annotation.surface: Someone who stated they backed a leader now withdrawing that support.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive but stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: aid, as a noun, is help or support given to someone.

entries.clue: Intend to capture marine creature not truly of the sea (6)

definitions.text: creature not truly of the sea

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it, so MEAN holds RM inside it

annotation.surface: Someone planning to catch a sea creature that doesn't really belong to the sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marine creature' looks like one phrase but splits: marine is RM, creature starts the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a merman lives in the sea only in legend, so it is a creature not truly of the sea because it is not real.

entries.clue: Poor works in dodgy sci-fi causing one to crash (9)

indicators.note: to work something is to shape or knead it, so POOR is reshaped
one thing in another sits inside it, so the reshaped POOR goes inside the other
dodgy means unreliable, so SCIFI's letters cannot be trusted to stay put

annotation.surface: A review of bad science fiction that sends viewers to sleep.
annotation.walkthrough: Crash here is slang for falling asleep, not a collision.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang sense: to crash is to fall fast asleep, and something soporific induces sleep.

entries.clue: Guarantee bit of pork trimmed by butcher showing skill with blade (9)

indicators.note: a trim runs round the edge of a garment, so SLAY forms the border around WORD and P

blocks.note: to give your word is to guarantee

annotation.surface: A butcher proving deft with a knife by trimming pork.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sets up a butcher's knife, and the definition is about blades too, but it means fencing.
annotation.definitionFit: Swordplay is fencing or sword fighting, the art of handling a blade well.

entries.clue: Theatrical work, elevated work about soldier (5)

indicators.note: raised up; in a down clue that means read from bottom to top
about means around, so PO goes around ANT

blocks.note: OP (opus, a work), written upwards as PO

annotation.surface: A description of a lofty play about a soldier.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter uses 'work' twice: once inside the definition, once as OP. Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show for families, full of slapstick and audience shouting.
annotation.definitionFit: Panto is the informal short form of pantomime, a kind of theatrical production.

entries.clue: Danger: IT could become a significant part of our universe (3,5)

definitions.text: a significant part of our universe

indicators.note: letters that could become something else are turned into a new word by rearranging

annotation.surface: A warning that information technology might take over the cosmos.
annotation.walkthrough: IT in capitals looks like information technology but is simply two letters of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a red giant is a huge ageing star, and stars are a sizeable part of the universe.

entries.clue: Imminent and taking shape, involving most of the firm (11)

indicators.note: to involve is to include within, so FORMING takes THCO inside
most of a word is all but its last letter, so THE becomes TH

annotation.surface: A company plan about to materialise, with most of the firm involved.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Most of' applies only to 'the', not to the whole firm.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: forthcoming describes what is about to appear or happen, which is what imminent means.

entries.clue: Pitch marker clubs abandoned abruptly (4)

indicators.note: something ended abruptly is cut short, so LEFT loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A golf pitch where the clubs were left behind in a hurry.
annotation.walkthrough: Pitch and clubs suggest sport; the pitch is musical.
annotation.definitionFit: A clef is the symbol at the start of a stave that fixes the pitch of the notes, so it marks pitch.

entries.clue: Cover, scarlet, that is turned over blue (9)

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped end to end, so RED and IE are read backwards together

annotation.surface: A red bedspread flipped over to show a blue side.
annotation.walkthrough: Blue reads as a colour beside scarlet, but it means low in spirits.
annotation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt stuffed with duck down, a bed cover.

entries.clue: Lament opening of electricity network being put back (5)

indicators.note: put back means sent backwards, so E and GRID are read in reverse

blocks.note: the electricity grid is a network

annotation.surface: Grief over the power grid's launch being postponed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put back' reads as delayed but tells you to reverse EGRID.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a dirge is a mournful song for the dead, a lament.

entries.clue: Tongue, European tongue, coming about with formality (4,3,6)

blocks.note: a spit is a tongue of land

annotation.surface: Two languages being spoken on a formal occasion.
annotation.walkthrough: Both tongues suggest languages, but the first is a spit, a narrow tongue of land jutting into water.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from military boot-cleaning: spit and polish means great attention to smart appearance and ceremony, i.e. formality.

entries.clue: Mischief over US city blues I played? Unlikely (11)

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing over another sits above it, so IMP comes first
notes played are performed in a new arrangement, so BLUESI is rearranged

blocks.note: a mischief is a naughty child, an imp

annotation.surface: A musician doubting they played the blues in an American city.
annotation.walkthrough: Mischief is used in its concrete sense, a mischievous child, rather than the behaviour.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: implausible means not easy to believe, hence unlikely.

entries.clue: Allegedly and conceivably dropping No 1, retaining rest of soccer team? (10)

indicators.note: the number one letter is the first, and dropping it leaves OSSIBLY
to retain is to keep hold of, so OSSIBLY holds TEN inside

blocks.note: possibly = conceivably; minus its first letter
a soccer side is eleven; take away one and ten remain

annotation.surface: A report on a football team with its first-choice player dropped.
annotation.walkthrough: No 1 hints at the goalkeeper's shirt but instructs removing the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: ostensibly means apparently, as stated, which is what allegedly conveys.

entries.clue: Fool expected to seize power (4)

indicators.note: to seize is to grab and hold, so DUE holds P inside

annotation.surface: An idiot who is predicted to take control.
annotation.walkthrough: Fool reads as a noun but works equally as a verb; dupe is both.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to dupe is to trick, and a dupe is a person tricked, a fool.

entries.clue: Those opposing going round hobbling birds (10)

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it, so FOES surrounds LAMING

annotation.surface: Enemies circling and injuring birds.
annotation.walkthrough: Flamingoes famously stand on one leg, which makes 'hobbling birds' a neat touch.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: flamingoes are pink wading birds.

entries.clue: Lecture, perhaps, has Mike working with introduction, extracting press release (9)

indicators.note: to extract is to pull out, so PR is pulled out of PROLOGUE

blocks.note: Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A talk that a man called Mike gives with an introduction but no press release.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the lecture as one example of a monologue.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a lecture is one speaker talking at length, a kind of monologue.

entries.clue: A drinking challenge knocking out one European in Welsh town (8)

indicators.note: to knock out is to remove, so one E is struck from BEER

blocks.note: E = European; one of BEER's two Es goes

annotation.surface: A drinking dare in Wales that ends with a foreign visitor knocked out.
annotation.walkthrough: Aberdare is a town in the South Wales valleys; the Welsh setting fits the drinking-game surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Aberdare is a real town in the Cynon Valley in south Wales.

entries.clue: Gorgeously-coloured insects surrounding a doctor heading for Oaxaca (10)

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose, so FLY ANT goes around A, MB and O

blocks.note: two insects: fly and ant, split FL…YANT

annotation.surface: Brightly coloured Mexican insects swarming around a doctor bound for Oaxaca.
annotation.walkthrough: Oaxaca is a Mexican state; only its O is used. The flamboyant is also a tropical tree with vivid red flowers.
annotation.definitionFit: Flamboyant describes something showy and vivid, and is especially used of brilliant colours.

entries.clue: I have to follow source of Government grant (4)

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so I'VE is written after G

annotation.surface: Someone awaiting a government grant.
annotation.walkthrough: Grant reads as a noun beside Government but is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to grant something is to give it formally.

entries.clue: Tried out adopting old computer program (6)

indicators.note: out means not in its proper state, so TRIED is disordered
to adopt is to take in, so O is added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Testing some old computer software.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tried out' reads as tested, but out is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a text editor is a program for writing and changing files.

entries.clue: What indicates senior officer took off immediately with bombs? (9,4)

blocks.note: fighter pilots scramble, taking off at once

annotation.surface: Fighter planes launching in a hurry carrying bombs.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sounds abstract but refers to a uniform detail; the wordplay is all air-force slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Service slang: scrambled eggs is the gold braid on the peak of a senior officer's cap, which marks rank.

entries.clue: Staff sell fruit (5)

annotation.surface: Shop workers selling fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: Staff reads as a noun for workers, but it is the verb: to man a stall.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the mango is a tropical stone fruit.

entries.clue: Pressure off agreements in items of legislation (4)

indicators.note: something off is detached, so the P comes away from PACTS

blocks.note: pacts are agreements; drop the P

annotation.surface: Pressure easing during treaty negotiations over new laws.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue starts with the letter to remove, before the word it comes from.
annotation.definitionFit: Laws passed by a parliament are called Acts, each one an item of legislation.

entries.clue: Emergency committee’s support led by army chief (5)

indicators.note: whatever leads goes in front, so CO comes before BRA

blocks.note: a bra is a support garment

annotation.surface: An emergency committee getting backing from the head of the army.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name: COBRA is the UK government's crisis committee, named after Cabinet Office Briefing Room A.

entries.clue: Entertainment venue near Bath opened by 10cc (9)

indicators.note: something opened by another is split to let it in, so TUB takes CL inside

blocks.note: 10 cubic centimetres is one centilitre, cl

annotation.surface: A music venue near the city of Bath launched by the rock band 10cc.
annotation.walkthrough: Bath is the English city and 10cc a 1970s band, but here bath is a tub and 10cc is a measure: one centilitre.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a nightclub is a place for late drinking, music and dancing.

entries.clue: Disrespect I found in recording (3)

indicators.note: something found in another is located inside it, so I sits within LP

annotation.surface: Someone discovering they were insulted on a tape.
annotation.walkthrough: Recording suggests a tape or video; the crossword standard is LP, a vinyl album.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal sense: lip is cheeky, insolent talk, as in 'don't give me any lip'.

entries.clue: Dockworker set aside nets day by day (9)

indicators.note: to net something is to catch it, so STORE catches EVE D inside
by means next to, so EVE sits beside D

blocks.note: to store is to set aside
an eve is the day before

annotation.surface: A docker putting away nets every single day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nets' reads as fishing gear on a dock but is a verb meaning catches.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a stevedore loads and unloads ships at the docks.

entries.clue: Respond, taking answer from second view (5)

indicators.note: taking something away removes it, so A comes out
from names the word it is taken out of, REPLAY

blocks.note: a replay lets you view something a second time

annotation.surface: Someone reacting after watching something again.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma splits definition from wordplay; 'answer' is the single letter A, not the solution.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to reply is to answer, to make a response.
